summary: Re-review of round 2. The r2 blocker is really fixed. Retriggered envelopes are anchored at the note: check-onsets passes for 22 instruments and 8 stingers, the stop fade measures -1.2 dB at 100 ms, there is no pre-sounded bass before GO in game, and race -> results is a ~0.75 s crossfade instead of a hard cut. Drums are now samples, so reversed hats are impossible. These r2 items are also fixed: the finish freeze plus finishLow for places 4-8 with the results song opening on B, the 2 s / 2-bar top-3 hysteresis, 2-minute title/menu/results loops with 8-bar bass lines per section, and the harmony nits (harmony-r3.json: no sustained clash left). Cymbals now use 808 metal partials and a stereo plate. Sloth barks are <= 2.4 s. ui.stamp/ui.count fire on results. The r2-tech items pass too: boot without WebAudio, restart/pause start sync, the mute check, voices pausing, trace-on-sound and WebKit suspend. tools/audio-check.mjs is fully green (offline + game, exit 0). Peaks are -1.1...-3.9 dBFS with 0 clicks. Loops are seamless. SFX coverage of SPEC 11 is complete (all 9 weapons, 11 skills, 9 animal calls, horns, siren/whistle, UI set) and event->sound latency is 0.1-3.6 ms. Unlock behaviour is correct: suspended and silent before the gesture, title theme on the first key, carried into the menus. KO / WRECKED / SHOWTIME are well choreographed: a +15 dB boom in 60-150 Hz, the top end muffled ~20 dB in slow-mo, the announcer at the peak and the whoosh back. Pause muffles hard and generic slow-mo muffles proportionally. Voice files match the manifest 92/92. It does not pass, for two reasons. (1) Mix/tonal balance (new): the wah/flute lead alone fills the 1 kHz octave as loud as kick+bass fill the 125 Hz octave, and in game the hook's octave is +1.7...+3.8 dB ABOVE the low end. The loops are pink-flat above 500 Hz where commercial mixes fall 3-5 dB/oct, the kick has little sub, and the image is near-mono (S/M -12.8...-16.9 dB). (2) Audio-thread CPU is still over budget (r2 major, improved, not fixed): race p50 6.3-6.4 %, pack 7-8 %, stretch 6.5-9.1 %, p90 8.7-12.3 %. A control graph reads 0.47 % at the same load. Minors: flat macro-dynamics (LRA 1.6-3.4 LU, breakdowns only -3 dB, builds that do not build), held barks always dropped in the short cinematics, square city/mountain hooks and flat coast hats, partial taunt coverage, and the cross-unit police sfx. Evidence: shots/review/audio/r3-music/ (audio-check-*.log, cpu-control.json, harmony-r3.json, coast-race.json + coast-*.wav, city-moments.json + city-*.wav, twoko.json, loop-*.flac renders, sections.py / analyze.py, sheet1.jpg, sheet2.jpg, spec-coast.png).

issues.title: Tonal balance: lead-dominated, honky 1 kHz and bright top over a thin low end (every song, in game too)
issues.detail: Full-loop offline renders through the real graph (render-loop.mjs, sections.py). The octave-band method is validated: pink noise reads flat. Octave bands relative to the 125 Hz octave, race-coast full mix: 63 -2.5, 250 -4.4, 500 -2.7, 1k -0.4, 2k -3.6, 4k -6.3, 8k -4.5, 14k -7.4. City: 1k -0.6. Mountain: 1k -1.8. Title: 1k -2.7. Results: 1k -0.4. Menu is flat 125-1k, then -12.5 at 2k. Per-stem (coast): the LEAD ALONE is -0.2 dB in the 1 kHz octave and -3.5 at 2 kHz, so it is the loudest single element in any band of the mix; the hats alone are -4.2 at 8 kHz. In game, with bike loops and sfx (coast-stretch.wav, city-slowmo.wav), the hook's 1 kHz octave sits +3.8 dB (coast stretch) and +1.7 dB (city) ABOVE the 125 Hz octave. Commercial funk/pop long-term spectra fall ~3-5 dB/oct above ~250 Hz (1 kHz octave ~8-12 dB and 8 kHz ~15-20 dB under the low octave). These loops are close to pink-flat, ~10 dB more mid/top than that. Causes: (a) the r1 'melody buried' fix overshot. The lead sits at -4 LU and the wah's sustain is a Q 3.8 band-pass parked at 1250 Hz (lead.ts), a narrow honk at vocal level. (b) Cymbals were raised +5.5...+7 dB. (c) The kick (drum-samples.ts: sine 165 -> 54 Hz in 65 ms, perc decay 0.34 s) is already ~15 dB down when it reaches its fundamental. Its 35-70 Hz peak is 6 dB under the bass, its spectral peak is at ~128 Hz, and the 63 Hz octave stays below 125 Hz in every song. On headphones or a TV this reads as a nasal, hissy demo mix, not a polished stylised-game soundtrack.
issues.fix:
Rebalance by spectrum instead of lead LU:
- Lead -3 dB (DEFAULT_MIX lead 0.85 -> ~0.6). Wah sustain: Q 3.8 -> ~2.2 and settle 1250 -> ~1700 Hz. Flute: raise the 2nd/3rd partials (0.12/0.04 -> ~0.3/0.12) so its energy spreads. Keep the hook clear by carving the masker (UNDER_LEAD_GAIN 0.67 -> 0.5, plus a ~1 kHz dip on keys/brass while the lead plays).
- Hats/ride/crash -3 dB.
- Kick: hold near full level ~40 ms, then decay over ~0.5 s so the 50-60 Hz body lands. Side-chain depth 0.42 -> ~0.3.
- Replace the 'lead -3.5...-7.5 LU' gate in audio-check with a loop-level tonal gate vs the 125 Hz octave: 1 kHz <= -6 dB, 8 kHz <= -10 dB, 63 Hz >= -1 dB. Keep the hook-clearance gate (>= +3 dB over its masker).

issues.title: Audio-thread CPU still over the 5 % budget (r2 major improved, not fixed)
issues.detail:
Two runs of the unit's own realtime gate (audio-check-cpu.log, audio-check-game.log; CDP renderCapacity, 1080p, machine load 9.9-15) against the budget p50 <= 5 %, p90 <= 8 %:
- race: p50 6.4 / 6.3 %, p90 9.4 / 8.7 %
- busy pack: p50 7.0 / 8.0 %, p90 10.6 / 10.3 %
- final stretch: p50 9.1 / 6.5 %, p90 12.3 / 8.8 %
- menu: 4.1-4.2 / 5.3-6.6 %
r2 measured race 8.0 / 10.5 and stretch 10.1 / 14.8, so this is ~20-35 % better, but still 1.3-1.8x over. A trivial 32 kHz oscillator graph in the same browser at the same load reads p50 0.47 % / p90 0.59 % (cpu-control.json), so machine load does not explain the overrun. The gate only stays green because overruns are downgraded to warnings when loadavg > cores; status itself lists C1 as STILL OPEN.
issues.fix: Pre-render brass stabs and pad chords per voicing, as already done for the Rhodes comping: stab envelopes are fixed shapes, so the cost becomes 1 source per chord. Build the stretch octave-double as a second oscillator into the same Lead filter/strip instead of a second Lead with its own band-pass and drive. Feed the bike loops through one shared gain stage. Make the CPU gate fail (not warn) whenever a control graph measured in the same run reads < 1 %, so the load excuse only applies when the meter is really inflated.

issues.title: Near-mono, centre-stacked image; brass and pad are one mono saw per note
issues.detail:
Side/mid energy and L/R correlation of the music bus over full loops (sections.py):
- coast: -12.8 dB / 0.90
- city: -16.4 / 0.96
- mountain: -16.9 / 0.96
- title: -15.4 / 0.94
- menu: -16.3 / 0.95
- results: -15.6 / 0.95
Per coast stem: lead -28 dB (reverb only), brass -27, clav -33, pad -21, bass mono. Only the drums (-8) and the keys auto-pan (-14) have width. band.ts gives no channel a pan except keys. brass.ts is 4 saws total (one per voicing note, mono, one filter) and keys.ts Pad is 4 saws, one per note, mono. So lead, brass, clav, pad and bass all fight in the centre, and the 'horn section' and pad sound like single thin synth voices next to a commercial funk/P5-style mix (typically S/M ~ -8...-10 dB with panned clav/guitar and wide horns).
issues.fix:
Spend a few nodes per Band (not per note):
- clav strip pan -0.35, lead2 octave double +0.25
- brass: voicing notes 1+3 -> pan -0.3, notes 2+4 -> +0.3 (two shared panners)
- pad saws alternating +/-0.45
- a 12-18 ms Haas send on the lead
Or render brass/pad chords as stereo buffers with two detuned takes L/R (this also serves the CPU fix). Target music-bus S/M ~ -10 dB, correlation ~0.8. Add it to the offline gate.

issues.title: Flat macro-dynamics: breakdowns barely dip and the 4-bar builds do not build
issues.detail: EBU R128 loudness range of the full loops is 1.6-3.4 LU: coast 2.9, city 2.6, mountain 3.4, title 2.6, menu 1.6, results 2.8. Section RMS of the loops stays within ~2.5 dB (coast A -20.9 ... S/B2 -18.6). Per bar, the D breakdown is only -2.7 dB under the end of S in coast and -3.1 dB in mountain. The 4-bar 'build' (D5-D8) is flat: coast -20.7 -> -20.6 dB, city -20.5 -> -20.3, mountain -22.9 -> -22.3, then a jump at B2. The spectrogram (spec-coast.png) shows the hats leaving for 4 bars while bass/keys/pad keep the same level. A commercial arrangement drops a breakdown 6+ dB and ramps the build into the drop. Here the 2-minute loops read as one constant wall, and the menu lounge song hardly breathes.
issues.fix: In D bars 1-4, keep only kick on 1 plus rim, take the bass to long notes at -4 dB, and sweep a band low-pass from ~800 Hz open across bars 5-8. Make the build snare roll a velocity crescendo (0.4 -> 1.0) with a riser and a +3...4 dB band ramp into B2 (Band.fade exists). Give menu/title A sections a lighter kit and comp than B2/A4. Gate: D bars 1-4 >= 6 dB under B2, a monotonic build, race-song LRA >= 4 LU.

issues.title: Held character lines are always dropped in the short cinematics (WRECKED, repeat KO)
issues.detail: events-combat.ts holds the KO barks until cine:ko end, but VoicePlayer.play() rejects barks until the announcer line ends + 0.25 s (busy.bark) and returns 'dropped'. Barks.say then neither retries nor falls back. When the player is wrecked (city-moments.json), the cinematic is start 0.52, peak 0.81, end 1.41 s, and ann_wrecked (0.54 s) blocks barks until 1.60 s. Result: no pelican_hurt line and no attacker gloat (status claims pelican_hurt_0 plays), and only silence follows the whoosh. Second KO 4 s after a first (twoko.json): the short variant goes peak 4.19 -> end 4.53 s while ann_ko blocks until ~4.85 s, so the victim's hurt line is dropped. The full-length KO works: pelican_ko_1 plays at the end.
issues.fix: In releaseBarks() (or VoicePlayer for channel 'bark'), schedule a held line at max(cine end, bark-block end), or queue one bark with a ~1.2 s stale limit instead of returning 'dropped'. Add audio-check cases: player wrecked -> pelican_hurt_* within 1 s of cine:ko end; repeat KO within 10 s -> the victim's hurt line sounds.

issues.title: Groove/hook details: square city/mountain hooks, machine-gun coast hats
issues.detail: Coast's hook is properly 16th-syncopated. The city flute hook (city.ts HOOK) and the mountain wah hook (mountain.ts HOOK), however, start almost every note on the 8th grid (mountain bar 1 onsets 0/4/6/8/10/14, city one 16th push in 8 bars). Leads have no legato glide between adjacent notes, only scoops, so the acid-jazz/funk hooks feel stiff. Coast H1 'xxOxxxOxxxOxxxOx' plays every closed 16th at the same velocity (0.8 +/- 6 %). The other songs alternate x/o accents, but the first race track has flat machine-gun hats under the whole A/A3/S groove.
issues.fix: Add 16th anticipations to the city/mountain hooks: push 1-2 notes per bar to the 'a' of a beat, e.g. city bar 1 'G5 - Bb5 - C6 - . Eb6 - D6 - C6 Bb5 - G5' with Eb6 anticipating beat 3. Add a 30-50 ms portamento in Lead.note when the previous note is still sounding. Coast H1 -> 'XoOoxoOoXoOoxoOo'-style accents (quarters strong, 16ths soft).

issues.title: Voices: most roster taunts still unvoiced; countdown words ~3 dB hotter than the set
issues.detail: public/assets/voice has 92 clips, matching the manifest 92/92, all 0.28-2.39 s with peaks <= -2.1 dBFS (sloth fixed). But only 34 of the 109 roster taunts have a clip, so ~2/3 of taunt bubbles get the animal call instead of a voice, and voiced vs honk-only bubbles alternate unpredictably. Active-speech RMS (frames > -50 dB): ann_1 -12.8, ann_2 -13.5, ann_3 -13.4, ann_go -13.3 dB vs -15.1...-17.0 for the other announcer lines. The whole-clip RMS match counts the tails, so the monosyllables still jump ~3 dB.
issues.fix: On the next IOA-VPN run, generate the remaining 75 taunts with node tools/gen-tts.mjs, which also rebuilds src/data/voice.ts. In gen-tts, RMS-match on active frames (> -50 dB) instead of the whole clip, so the countdown sits at the set's ~-16 dB.

issues.title: cross-unit: police horn/whistle/knock are still direct, unpositioned sfx() calls
issues.detail: gameplay/race/police.ts:127 calls app.audio.sfx('traffic.horn.police'), :144 calls sfx('police.whistle') and :157 calls sfx(<hit>). They play centred at full level wherever the corgi is, bypassing audio's placement and rate limits. The audio-side core request ('police:whistle' event) is filed in status/audio.md; this belongs to race and core.
issues.fix: core adds 'police:whistle' { riderId, pos } and race emits it, routing the corgi's knocks through combat:hit. Audio then places them like every other world sound.
